Read the comic as text
  1. A bug report

    The team learns that a registration was recorded twice just before release.

  2. Stop before production

    Failed registrations are increasing. The team decides to investigate before release.

  3. Work with SIMY

    “SIMY! Find the cause, fix it, and test it!” “First, I’ll reproduce it.”

  4. Find the cause

    A network error triggers duplicate retries: the same request is sent twice.

  5. Make a user-focused decision

    “An error clears the input. Keep it?” “Yes! Don’t waste the user’s time.”

  6. Go beyond the fix

    Fix, retest, and review with another AI. The team checks the test and review results.

  7. Decide from evidence

    Check changes, tests, reviews, user experience, and monitoring before deciding to deploy.

  8. Carry the lesson forward

    After deployment, the team celebrates and carries the lesson into the next development task.

02 / SQM (WEB): PREVENTION RULES

Turn “one registration per retry” into a code check.

Check duplicate prevention in the API and regression tests, beyond the form’s button controls.

Enlarge screen (new tab) ↗
  1. 1

    Risk: retries or repeated clicks create two registrations.

  2. 2

    Requirement: treat the same application as one; accept different applications normally.

  3. 3

    Verify identifier-based deduplication, concurrent requests, and no false blocking of different applications.

Rule configuration example, not actual detection or test results.

03 / SQM (WEB): CHECK SCOPE

Beyond the form: API and storage too.

Preventing duplicates requires understanding the path from the form through acceptance and storage.

Enlarge screen (new tab) ↗
  1. 1

    Review the proposed scope before applying it to quality checks.

  2. 2

    See the relationships among form, API, storage, email, regression tests, and shared types.

01

Delegate development

Ask for a bug fix.
Get the code, tests, and review.

Connect investigation, implementation, testing, and review. When a check finds an issue, fix it and check again. Review the change alongside its results.

AN EXAMPLE REQUEST

“Fix duplicate submissions in the signup form. Check recovery from errors, too.”

WHAT YOU RECEIVE

The code change, test results, and review findings. You decide whether to release.
